questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a place that had the same level of education as UCPH but that also had a very different culture that I could explore.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The really necessary information is very available, but some other information that is nice to know is not that easy find and which you will have to discover yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little. You pretty much have to get situated yourself. There are some mails that will tell you what you need to do, but even they can be a bit vague at times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation is good for meeting other exchange students but the local students that are showing you around don't always know what they are supposed to do or might just leave halfway through. You, therefore, don't get a lot of useful information through the orientation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a large amount of variety in university housing, but you don't have much choice in what you get through the application form. You also aren't certain to get anything so if you are offered something it is a good idea to take it pretty much no matter what the offer is.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You are required to get a meal plan. They are quite expensive and in my case almost useless because my housing is a bit away from the actual campus where all the food spots are. Most of the food offeres is also fast food which becomes a bit much after a while. The meal plan is also pretty expensive and you don't get your money back if you don't use it all. Depending on your housing you have different cooking facilities. I had a stove and oven, but I then had to get everything else for the kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive. Though it is probably even more expensive finding your own appartment outside of university. You also have to be ok with sharing a pretty small room with other peopl since this is how most of the housing is. It is rare to get a single unit.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is not that nice for the price you pay for it but that is how it is in New York.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to get waivers for the pre requisites for courses. You do this by filling out a form that they send you and then they will get back to you if they believe you to have the needed background knowledge for the courses you want to take. There are three rounds of this that you can do and only one of them is before registration starts. It is therefore good to try to do that one as well as possible so that you don't risk some of your courses filling up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Very little. They give you the general approach but then it is up to you and you having to be good at pursuing them, because they can be tremendously slow at getting back to you. So don't be afraid of writing them to push them to get through the forms.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of the classes I wanted got cancelled, but I was able to register for all the other ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start preparing early so you are ready for the first round of forms to get waivers so that your classes don't fill up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The Bachelor's courses are slightly easier than what you would expect at UCPH while the Master's courses would fit as fairly difficult third year Bachelor's courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is quite different. The classes are much smaller and I never spent any time in a lecture hall. Recitations are also just more lectures in a sense. Also pretty much everything counts towards your final grade and there are know practice problems that you will get that are just meant to help you improve.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational Physics
General Relativity
Classical and Quantum Mechanics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially recommend GR and CQM they had very good teachers and I learned a lot. Though if you don't study physics or something related they are probably not for you.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries are very expensive as is the meal plan that they require you to get if you live in university housing. Housing is also incredibly expensive though I did end up getting offered one of the more expensive packages. Also things like housing and the meal plan have to be paid all at once before the semester or in installments throughout the semester, but if you do it in installements then there is added interest.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Consumer goods are much cheaper in America, however, pretty much everything you need in your daily life is more expensive here. Especially food and housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much anything you could want. Look at NYU Engage for a list of all of the clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The NYU Run Club is very good. It is both very social and you get to do some activities with them if you want.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city. There is much to do and many cool places if you just go looking for them. There are also many great museums like the Met or MoMA.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. NYU is very strict with there rules and some of the rules are very vague. This is the thing to be most on the lookout for since you can easily find yourself in a situation where you have broken a rule completely unaware that you are doing so.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: That is easy to do in New York. Americans are very open to talking so if you just talk back then it's no problem. The clubs are also a great opportunity to meet new local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Again the very strict rule following. There is very little sense of looking at people like individuals and taking into account that they are from a different country and culture. It can therefore sometimes feel like an unwelcoming place because they can be very accusatory at times for the slightest violation of a rule that is not communicated.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How much is going on in the city. There is always something to do or see if you just go looking for it. And there are almost always someone to go do it or see it with.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join a club. It is a great way of socializing and meeting new friends especially among local students.
Say yes to everything. Try to do as much as possible. Especially in the beginning so that you will meet new people and see new things at a time where you don't know anyone in the city.
Don't only focus on academics. Give yourself some space to also enjoy that you are in New York and that you are able to go see the Met or walk by the Hudson anytime you want.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Practically it's all about being prepared and early so that everything goes a smoothly as possible. The American systems can be difficult at times so it helps if you are prepared.
Socially you've just got to say yes to as many new experiences as possible. These are the things that you will really appreciate about your trip when you are done.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people. It has been very rewarding meeting both exchange and local students. Delving into different cultures and seeing how life goes on in another country by talking with people from that country is extremely interesting and rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first month can feel very long. It takes a while getting settled in. Also because UCPH sends so few people to NYU you will most likely not know anyone here. It therefore take a bit before you get yourself some new friends that you can properly do things with. However, after that first month things really heat up and you start getting the most out of your stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
